## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
One defect needs fixing before merge. The pull request description promises that `--json` can use its default destination alongside `--junit`, but the new parser treats any token after `--json` as its path, including the next flag. As a result, `--json --junit out.xml` fails to parse, and in a related case JSON is written to a file named `--junit`.

## Critical
- app/cli.py:15 — correctness — Given `["--json", "--junit", "out.xml"]`, `parse_args` sets the JSON destination to `"--junit"` and then raises `ValueError("unknown option: out.xml")`, so the default destination cannot be combined with a following flag. Lines 15–19 accept `args[i + 1]` whenever it exists, without the `startswith("--")` check that the `--junit` branch uses at line 7. A related input, `["--json", "--junit"]`, returns `{"json": "--junit"}`, so `write_reports` writes the JSON report to a file literally named `--junit`. Recommended fix: keep the default unless the next argument exists and does not start with `--`, for example `if i + 1 < len(args) and not args[i + 1].startswith("--"): destination = args[i + 1]; i += 1`. Also add a test for `["--json", "--junit", "x.xml"]` that expects `{"json": "results.json", "junit": "x.xml"}`. — Users who put `--json` before `--junit`, the combination the PR body describes, get a parse error or a stray JSON file named after the flag. The existing test only covers `--json` as the last argument, so it does not catch this.
